items.problem: A UWP `DataTemplate x:DataType="local:Scenario"` with `{x:Bind}` failed markup compile (WMC0909 'Cannot resolve DataType local:Scenario' + WMC1111 'DataTemplates containing x:Bind need a DataType'). The agent recovered by switching the template to classic `{Binding}`.
items.evidence: session-log.txt ~2246-2247 (WMC0909/WMC1111), ~2299 ('XAML can't resolve local:Scenario with x:DataType — need to use {Binding} instead'), ~2305 (edit to `{Binding Title}`).
items.covered_at: MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md, section `### x:Bind and compiled bindings` (~line 683): 'x:Bind is supported... Compiled bindings against Windows.UI.Xaml.* types resolve... If the build emits XLS0414/MC3074 "type was not found", look for stale UWP namespace prefixes.'
items.proposed_improvement: Extend the existing x:Bind section to cover the DataTemplate case: when a `DataTemplate x:DataType="local:..."` fails with WMC0909/WMC1111 (often alongside WMC1509 'No LocalAssembly parameter'), the pragmatic fix is to fall back to classic `{Binding}` (runtime binding, no x:DataType needed). Keep it a short addition to the existing paragraph, not a new topic.
items.generalizes: UWP universal-sample shells (and many list-driven UWP apps) routinely author `ListBox/ListView` item templates as `DataTemplate x:DataType="local:..."` + `{x:Bind}` over project-local model types. This exact template pattern recurs across scenarios, so documenting the WMC0909/WMC1111 recovery generalizes broadly.
